text: Gratiam et pacem a Deo Patre nostro, et Domino Jesu Christo.
note: *Grātiam* capital: the greeting opens its own sentence after the address of 1:1 (as 1 Cor 1:3); *Patre* capital, God the Father (decision 20; *nostrō* lower case), as Rom 1:7 and 1 Cor 1:3 (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Collaudandus Deus et Pater Domini nostri Jesu Christi, misericordiae Pater, et omnis consolationis Deus,
note: *Pater* capital twice, God the Father (decision 20; NRSV "the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies"), as Rom 15:6 *Patrem Dominī nostrī* (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Nolumus enim vos ignorare, fratres, quanta adflictione, et quam omnino viribus nostris majore pressi fuerimus in Asia, usque adeo, ut etiam de vita dubitaremus.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 1:7 ends a sentence and Paul turns to his affliction in Asia, in direct address (*frātrēs*); *Nōlumus enim vōs ignōrāre* opens a new step, as Rom 1:13 and 1 Cor 10:1 (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Hoc igitur deliberans, numquid levitate usus sum? aut quae delibero, humano more delibero, ut sit apud me “etiam, etiam”: et “non, non”?
note: the words *etiam, etiam* and *nōn, nōn* quoted as words (the subject of *sit*: "that with me there be Yes, yes and No, no"), as the BSB and NRSV; lower case, words named, not a sentence spoken; the colon and question mark are Paul's, outside (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Fidelis est Deus, quod nostra ad vos oratio non fuit “etiam,” et “non.”
note: *etiam* and *nōn* quoted as words (the predicate of *fuit*), as 1:17 and the BSB; comma and full stop inside, as 1 Cor 14:16 *“Āmēn,”* (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Nam Dei Filius Jesus Christus, qui apud vos per nos praedicatus est, per me, et Sylvanum, et Timotheum, non fuit “etiam,” et “non”: sed in eo fuit “etiam.”
note: *Fīlius* capital, the Son of God (decision 20), as 1 Cor 1:9 *Fīliī*; *etiam*, *nōn* quoted as words as 1:17-18 and the BSB (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Omnes enim Dei promissiones tales sunt, ut in eo sit “etiam,” et in eo sit “ita,” quae res Deo sit gloriae per nos.
note: *etiam* and *ita* (Castellio's rendering of the Amen, ἀμήν) quoted as words, as the BSB's "Yes" and "Amen" and 1:17-19 (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: is qui nos consignavit, et Spiritus arrhabonem nostris animis indidit.
note: *Spīritūs* capital, the Holy Spirit given as the pledge (NRSV "his Spirit in our hearts"; decision 20); *is* lower case as the pipeline set it (the sentence runs on from 1:21) (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Quod si quis contristavit, non me contristavit nisi aliquatenus, ne vos omnes onerem.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 2:4 ends a sentence; a new topic, the offender and his forgiveness (2:5-11) (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Deo vero gratia, qui semper facit, ut in Christi negotio triumphemus, ejusque cognitionis odorem per nos divulgat omnibus in locis.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 2:13 ends a sentence; the narrative of Troas breaks off for the thanksgiving that opens the defence of Paul's ministry (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Estque perspicuum, vos esse Christi epistolam, a nobis administratam, non atramento, sed viventis Dei Spiritu descriptam, non in lapideis, sed in carneis animi tabulis.
note: *Spīritū* capital, the Spirit of the living God (NRSV "with the Spirit of the living God"; decision 20) (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: qui nos idoneos reddidit novi foederis ministros, non litterae, sed spiritus: nam littera perimit, at Spiritus vivificat.
note: as the NRSV ("not of letter but of spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life"): *spīritūs* against *litteræ* lower case, the second *Spīritus* capital (decision 20); *quī* lower case as the pipeline set it (3:5 ends with a comma) (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Nonne magis Spiritus ministerium erit cum splendore conjunctum?
note: *Spīritūs* capital, "the ministry of the Spirit" (NRSV; decision 20) (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Dominus autem Spiritus est: ubi vero Domini Spiritus est, ibi est libertas.
note: *Spīritus* capital twice, as the NRSV ("Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is") and the BSB (decision 20) (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Nos vero omnes detecta facie splendorem Domini speculantes, in eamdem transformamur imaginem, splendore perpetuando, tamquam a Domini Spiritu.
note: *Spīritū* capital, as the NRSV ("from the Lord, the Spirit") and 3:17 (decision 20) (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Quorum videlicet infidentium mentes caecavit hujus saeculi deus, ne collustret eos claritas gloriosi Christi evangelii, qui est imago Dei inadspectabilis.
note: *deus* lower case: "the god of this age" is Satan (1573's margin glosses it *diabolus*; NRSV "the god of this world"), not God (decision 20); *Deī* at the end stays capital. *Quōrum* keeps its capital after 4:3's colon, as the settled books do after a colon (1 Cor 41 : 1, Rom 54 : 1) (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Ac eodem fiduciae spiritu praediti, ut fert scriptum illud: \\qt “Credidi, ideoque locutus sum”\\qt*: nos quoque credimus, ideoque loquimur,
note: Ps 116:10 after *ut fert scrīptum illud:* in \\qt with “…”, prose as the BSB; the words are direct (first person), *Crēdidī* capital as the quotation's first word (1573 *Credidi*); the colon is Paul's, outside (as Rom 9:7). *fīdūciæ spīritū* lower case: "the same spirit of faith" (NRSV), not the Holy Spirit (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Hanc ob caussam non defetiscimur, quin etiamsi exterior noster homo corrumpatur, at interior quidem renovatur in dies.
note: a new paragraph, as the BSB: 4:15 ends a sentence and *Hanc ob causam nōn dēfetīscimur* draws the conclusion, taking up 4:1 (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Qui vero nos ad hoc ipsum fecit, Deus est, is qui nobis Spiritus arrhabonem dedit.
note: *Spīritūs* capital: the pledge God gives is the Holy Spirit (NRSV "the Spirit as a guarantee"; decision 20), as the same phrase at 1:22 should be (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Itaque quum pro Christo legatione fungamur, ut Deo per nos adhortante, quaesumus pro Christo, reconciliamini Deo,
note: a new paragraph, as the BSB: 5:19 ends a sentence and *Itaque* turns to the appeal; *reconciliāminī Deō* is Paul's own plea to his readers, so no quotation marks (the BSB has none either) (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Dicit enim: \\q1 \\qt “Te accepto tempore exaudivi,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt tibi die salutis subveni.”\\qt* \\m Adest nunc tempus acceptum, adest nunc dies salutis.
note: Isa 49:8 after *Dīcit enim:* as poetry in \\qt, two lines after the BSB (the Latin's order matches); *Tē* capital, the quotation's first word (1573 *Te*); *Adest nunc …* is Paul's comment, prose again inside the verse with \\m (as the BSB, and Gen 48:20) (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: in vigiliis, in jejuniis, in castitate, in scientia, in clementia, in benignitate, in Spiritu Sancto, in caritate genuina,
note: *Spīritū Sānctō* both capital, as every *Sānctus Spīritus* in the settled books (none lower case); the NRSV reads "holiness of spirit" here, but Castellio's words are the name, as the Vulgate's, the KJV's and the BSB's ("the Holy Spirit"); the least certain capital in 4–6 (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Os nostrum ad vos apertum est, Corinthii: animus noster largus est.
note: a new paragraph, as the BSB: 6:10 ends the long sentence of 6:4–10 and Paul turns to direct address (*Corinthiī*) (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Quae Dei templo cum deastris convenientia? Vos enim viventis Dei templum estis, quemadmodum dixit Deus: \\q1 \\qt “Habitabo ac versabor apud eos,\\qt* \\q1 \\qt eroque eorum Deus,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt et ipsi mihi populus erunt.\\qt*
note: Lev 26:12 (Ezek 37:27) after *quemadmodum dīxit Deus:* as poetry in \\qt; three lines, not the BSB's four, as Castellio joins "dwell" and "walk" in one clause (*habitābō ac versābor apud eōs*), so q1 q1 q2 (as Rom 14:11); *Habitābō* capital, the quotation's first word (1573 *Habitabo*). One quotation over 6:16–18, not closed here: *Quāpropter* (6:17) and *Vōbīsque* (6:18) join the next sayings with no new formula, and the *inquit* tags inside them name the same speaker (as Rom 9:25–26; the BSB closes and reopens) (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: \\qt Quapropter exite ex medio eorum,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt ac separamini,”\\qt* inquit Dominus: \\q1 \\qt “neve impurum tangite:\\qt* \\q2 \\qt et ego vos accipiam.\\qt*
note: Isa 52:11 (with Ezek 20:34), continuing the quotation of 6:16, as poetry in \\qt, four lines after the BSB; *inquit Dominus* is the tag, outside the marks and not italic (as Rom 12:19, 1 Cor 14:21), the quotation reopened after it; *nēve* lower case after the colon, the same sentence (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: \\qt Vobisque pater ero\\qt* \\q2 \\qt et vos mihi eritis filii ac filiae,”\\qt* \\q2 inquit Dominus omnipotens.
note: 2 Sam 7:14 (with 7:8), the quotation of 6:16–17 closed here; poetry in \\qt as the BSB, *inquit Dominus omnipotēns* on its last line outside the marks (as 1 Cor 14:21); no `m` (the poetry runs on from 6:17). *pater* lower case, a predicate (NRSV "I will be your father"); *omnipotēns* an adjective (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Admittite nos: nemini injuriam fecimus, neminem corrupimus, neminem circumscripsimus.
note: new paragraph (the BSB's b m): 7:1 closes the exhortation of 6:14–7:1 with a full stop, and *Admittite nōs* turns to direct appeal and opens Paul's joy over the Corinthians (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Quemadmodum scriptum exstat: \\q1 \\qt “Neque qui plus collegerat, plus habebat:\\qt* \\q2 \\qt neque qui minus collegerat, minus habebat.”\\qt*
note: Exod 16:18 after *scrīptum exstat:*: poetry in \\qt mid-verse, two lines after the BSB (as 1 Cor 1:19); *Neque* capital as the quotation's first word; the colon between the lines is Castellio's (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Misimus autem una cum eo fratrem, qui praeterquam quod in re evangelica per omnes laudatur ecclesias,
note: new paragraph (the BSB's b m): 8:17 ends with a full stop and *Mīsimus autem* opens a new step, the brother sent with Titus (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Ceterum et qui parce seret, parce etiam metet: et qui large seret, large etiam metet:
note: new paragraph (the BSB's b m): 9:5 ends with a full stop and *Cēterum* opens the principle of sowing and reaping; the proverb is Paul's own, unmarked as in the BSB (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Quemadmodum scriptum exstat: \\q1 \\qt “Quum dispergat, et pauperibus largiatur,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt ejus liberalitas manet aeterna.”\\qt*
note: Ps 112:9 after *scrīptum exstat:*: poetry in \\qt mid-verse, two lines after the BSB; *Quum* capital as the quotation's first word; Castellio's subordinate *quum* clause is his rendering of the psalm (finite verbs, *manet* indicative), so quoted, not reported (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Qui vero serenti et semen et panem ad victum suppeditat, is vobis semen suppeditet, multiplicetque, ac vestrae liberalitatis proventus sic augeat,
note: prose again after the poetry of 9:9 (the BSB's m) (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Deum collaudantes, tum ob vestram, qui in Christi evangelium concordes sitis, obedientiam, et simplicem in eos inque omnes largitatem:
note: *Deum* keeps its capital (God, as everywhere in the settled text), though the sentence runs on from 9:12's comma; the pipeline's lower case is for a common word (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Rerum speciem spectatis? Si quis sibi persuasit, se esse Christi: hoc rursum per sese cogitet, ut ipse Christi est, sic nos quoque esse Christi.
note: the BSB's ordinary break: 10:6 ends a sentence and Paul turns to address the readers with a question, a new step (who belongs to Christ) (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: quod “epistolae quidem (inquit) graves fortesque sunt, at corporis praesentia imbecilla, oratioque abjecta est.”
note: the critic's words, marked by *inquit* and kept in the indicative (*sunt … est*), as direct speech in “…” as the BSB; *quod* (because) outside and lower case (10:9 ends with a comma); the parenthesis *(inquit)* inside the marks as settled Exod 11:8 and 14:4 (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: \\qt “Qui vero gloriatur, in Domino glorietur.”\\qt*
note: Jer 9:24 (the BSB quotes it), the words 1 Cor 1:31 settled in \\qt: \\qt with “…”, prose; no formula here, so *Quī* capital; *vērō* stays inside (as *enim* at 1 Cor 2:16) (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: An peccatum admisi, meipsum demittens, ut vos extolleremini, quod vos gratis divinum evangelium docui?
note: the BSB's ordinary break: 11:6 ends a sentence and 11:7 opens a new step with a question (preaching without pay); *docuī?* with a question mark, as 1573 (*Euangelium docui ?*, canvas 885), for Wikisource's full stop (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Ac quod facio, facturusque sum, id facio, ut occasionem iis adimam, qui occasionem captant, quo sibi, in quo glorientur, suppetat, quemadmodum et nobis.
note: the BSB's ordinary break: 11:11 ends with *Scit Deus.* and 11:12 turns to the false apostles (11:12–15) (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Scit Deus et Pater Domini nostri Jesu Christi, qui est collaudandus in sempiternum, me non mentiri.
note: *Pater* capital, God the Father (decision 20), as Rom 15:6 *Deum, et Patrem Dominī nostrī* (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: “Satis est tibi mea gratia: nam mea fortitudo in imbecillitate perficitur.” Itaque multo libentissime gloriabor in meis debilitatibus, ut habitet in me fortitudo Christi.
note: the Lord's answer, introduced by 12:8's *sed ille mihi sīc dīxit:*, is direct speech (first person, *mea grātia*, *mea fortitūdō*): in “…”, *Satis* capital; it ends after *perficitur*, as the BSB (the *nam* clause is still the Lord's: *mea fortitūdō*), and *Itaque …* is Paul's again (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Jam tertium paratus sum visere vos, neque tamen vos exsugam. Non enim vestra, sed vos expeto. Nec enim debent liberi parentibus congerere, sed parentes liberis.
note: paragraph added: after 12:13's full stop Paul turns from his defence to his coming third visit (*Jam tertium parātus sum*; the BSB's b m) (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: An rursum putatis, vobis excusare nos? In Dei conspectu per Christum loquimur, et omnia, o carissimi, pro vestra utilitate facimus.
note: paragraph added: after 12:18's question Paul turns to address them directly about the purpose of all he has said (*ō cārissimī*; the BSB's b m); *vōbīs excūsāre nōs* is accusative and infinitive, unmarked (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Jam tertio venturus sum ad vos: \\qt “Ex duorum triumve testium ore decernetur de omni re.”\\qt*
note: Deut 19:15 (the BSB quotes it) in \\qt with “…”, prose as the BSB; no formula, the quotation follows Paul's colon as its own sentence, so *Ex* capital (as 1Cor 3:19 *Quī* after a colon); the same words at Matt 18:16 are woven into Jesus' *ut* clause and unmarked there (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Vos ipsos pertentate, an sitis fide praediti: vos ipsos explorate: annon vos ipsos eos agnoscitis, in quibus sit Jesus Christus? nisi forte rejectanei estis.
note: paragraph added: after 13:4's full stop Paul turns the test on them in direct commands (*Vōs ipsōs pertemptāte*; the BSB's b m) (Claude, 2026-11-10)

text: Domini Jesu Christi gratia, et Dei amor, et Sancti Spiritus communio vobis adsit omnibus. Amen. \\cls Ad Corinthios secunda scripta est Philippis Macedoniae, missa per Titum et Lucam.
note: the subscription set apart as \\cls after the verse (decision 37), as 1573 sets it in italics under the blessing (canvas 887) and as Rom 16:27 and 1 Cor 16:24; *Sānctī Spīritūs* both capital, as every *Sānctus Spīritus* in the settled books (decision 20); *omnibus.* with a full stop before *Āmēn*, as 1573 (*vobis adsit omnibus. Amen.*) and 1 Cor 16:24, for the draft's colon (Claude, 2026-11-10)
